summary: Generic label management service that creates labels, attaches and detaches them from application objects by type-scoped string identity, and exposes search, reverse-lookup, batch-read, and grouped-object query capabilities to any Atlas application.

classification.why_platform: LabelEngine provides reusable label primitives — creation, attachment, search, grouping — without encoding any application-specific business rules. It stores and retrieves labels by generic (object_id, object_type) addressing, leaving domain meaning entirely to consuming applications.
non_goals: Label schema validation or type enforcement beyond non-empty name
Interpretation of object_type semantics — that belongs to each application

consumes: Shared Atlas Postgres instance (02_Platform/Postgres) — connection via DATABASE_URL or ATLAS_PG_* environment variables
labels.labels table (id text PK, name text NOT NULL, created_at timestamptz)
labels.object_labels table (object_id text, label_id text FK, object_type text lowercase-constrained, attached_at timestamptz) — composite PK (object_id, label_id)
platform_errorhandling — optional; structured logging, exception handlers, request timing (install_exception_handlers, install_request_timing, setup_logging)
provides: HTTP API: GET /api/labels?q=<prefix> — case-insensitive prefix label search; empty q returns all labels ordered by name ASC
HTTP API: GET /api/labels/used?object_type=<str> — all distinct labels attached to at least one object of the given type, ordered by name ASC
HTTP API: POST /api/labels — create a named label; returns 201 LabelRecord
HTTP API: GET /api/objects/{object_id}/labels — all labels attached to an object, ordered by attached_at ASC then label_id ASC
HTTP API: POST /api/objects/{object_id}/labels — attach a label to an object by name; creates the label inline if not found; idempotent
HTTP API: DELETE /api/objects/{object_id}/labels/{label_id} — detach a label from an object; returns 204
HTTP API: POST /api/objects/labels/batch — return labels for up to 200 objects in one call, scoped by object_type; zero-fills missing entries
HTTP API: GET /api/groups?object_type=<str>&page=<int>&page_size=<int> — objects of a type grouped by primary label, paginated; named groups alphabetically then Unlabeled last
HTTP API: GET /health — liveness check, returns {status: ok}
invariants: Label names are matched case-insensitively for search and attach operations; 'Tag' and 'tag' resolve to the same label
Label name must be non-empty after stripping whitespace; enforced at API layer and by DB CHECK constraint
object_type must be lowercase; enforced by DB CHECK constraint (object_labels_object_type_lowercase)
Attachment is idempotent: POST /api/objects/{object_id}/labels returns the canonical ObjectLabelRecord whether the attachment is new or pre-existing
Primary label for an object is the label with the earliest attached_at; ties broken by label_id ASC
GET /api/objects/{object_id}/labels returns labels ordered by attached_at ASC, label_id ASC — consistent with primary-label ordering
Batch read zero-fills: every requested object_id appears as a key in the response dict even if it has no labels
GET /api/groups pagination is over the flat object list before grouping; meta.total = unpaginated distinct object count; meta.page_count = ceil(total / page_size)
Named groups are returned alphabetically; the Unlabeled group (objects with no labels in this type scope) is always appended last
GET /api/labels and GET /api/labels/used both order results by lower(name) ascending
GET /api/labels/used returns an empty list (not 404) when no labels are attached to any object of the given type
Schema is initialised idempotently at startup via CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
failure_modes: OBJECT_TYPE_REQUIRED (422): object_type query param is absent or blank after strip — GET /api/labels/used, POST /api/objects/{object_id}/labels, GET /api/groups
LABEL_NAME_EMPTY (422): label name is blank after strip — POST /api/labels, POST /api/objects/{object_id}/labels
OBJECT_TYPE_INVALID (422): object_type contains uppercase characters — triggers DB CHECK constraint violation on insert
LABEL_NOT_FOUND (404): label_id supplied to DELETE does not exist in labels.labels
ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND (404): (object_id, label_id) pair does not exist in labels.object_labels on DELETE
BATCH_TOO_LARGE (422): object_ids list in batch request exceeds 200 items
Database connectivity failure propagates as unhandled 500 (platform_errorhandling exception handler will format it as ApiError if installed)

provides: LabelRecord: {id: str, name: str}
ObjectLabelRecord: {object_id: str, label_id: str, label_name: str, attached_at: str (ISO-8601)}
BatchLabelRecord: {id: str, name: str, attached_at: str (ISO-8601)}
GroupItem: {id: str, primary_label: str | None, labels: list[str]}
LabelGroup: {label: str, items: list[GroupItem]}
GroupedMeta: {total: int, page: int, page_size: int, page_count: int}
LabelSearchResponse: {labels: list[LabelRecord]}
ObjectLabelsResponse: {labels: list[ObjectLabelRecord]}
GroupedObjectsResponse: {meta: GroupedMeta, groups: list[LabelGroup]}
BatchLabelsRequest: {object_ids: list[str], object_type: str}
BatchLabelsResponse: {labels: dict[str, list[BatchLabelRecord]]}

consumes: psycopg2 SimpleConnectionPool with RealDictCursor — connection acquired via get_db() context manager
provides: GET /api/labels?q=<str> — prefix label search; q defaults to empty (returns all)
GET /api/labels/used?object_type=<str> — reverse lookup of labels by object type; object_type required
POST /api/labels — body: {name: str}; returns 201 LabelRecord
GET /api/objects/{object_id}/labels — returns ObjectLabelsResponse
POST /api/objects/{object_id}/labels — body: {label_name: str, object_type: str}; returns 201 ObjectLabelRecord
DELETE /api/objects/{object_id}/labels/{label_id} — returns 204
POST /api/objects/labels/batch — body: {object_ids: list[str], object_type: str}; max 200 ids; returns BatchLabelsResponse
GET /api/groups?object_type=<str>&page=<int>&page_size=<int> — returns GroupedObjectsResponse; page defaults 1, page_size defaults 50
GET /health — returns {status: ok}

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Case-insensitive prefix search over all labels. Empty q returns all labels ordered by name ASC.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/labels/used
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return all distinct labels attached to at least one object of the given object_type, ordered by name ASC. Empty list if none; 422 if object_type absent.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Create a new label by name. Returns 201 LabelRecord. 422 if name is blank.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/objects/{object_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return all labels attached to object_id ordered by attached_at ASC, label_id ASC.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/objects/{object_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Attach a label to an object by name. Resolves or creates the label (case-insensitive). Idempotent. Requires object_type (lowercase). Returns 201 ObjectLabelRecord.

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/objects/{object_id}/labels/{label_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Detach a label from an object. Returns 204. 404 if label or attachment not found.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/objects/labels/batch
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return labels for up to 200 objects in one query, scoped by object_type. Zero-fills missing entries. 422 if object_type absent or object_ids exceeds 200.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/groups
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return objects of object_type grouped by primary label with pagination. Named groups alphabetically, Unlabeled last. 422 if object_type absent.

exposed_surfaces.name: LabelService
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Internal service class encapsulating all label business logic and SQL. Not exposed externally — consumed only by routers within LabelEngine.

internal_flow.name: request_validation
internal_flow.description: Router validates required parameters (object_type, label_name, object_ids). Blank or absent required params return 422 ApiError via _api_error helper before any DB interaction.
outputs: validated parameter values or 422 ApiError response

internal_flow.name: connection_acquisition
internal_flow.description: get_db() context manager acquires a psycopg2 connection from the SimpleConnectionPool. On exception, rolls back and returns the connection to the pool.

internal_flow.name: service_dispatch
internal_flow.description: Router calls the appropriate LabelService method. LabelService executes parameterized SQL queries against the labels schema. LabelEngineError is raised for known failure conditions (LABEL_NOT_FOUND, ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND). psycopg2 CheckViolation from the object_type lowercase constraint surfaces as OBJECT_TYPE_INVALID.

internal_flow.name: response_construction
internal_flow.description: Router returns the Pydantic response model (FastAPI serialises to JSON) or converts a LabelEngineError into an ApiError JSON response via _api_error. Mutation endpoints commit the connection inside the service method before returning.
outputs: HTTP response with appropriate status code and JSON body

internal_required.role: Shared Postgres instance — LabelEngine owns the 'labels' schema within it
Connection pool initialisation, schema init, get_db() context manager
LabelService — all business logic and SQL

internal_optional.role: Structured logging, FastAPI exception handlers, request timing — imported conditionally; service runs without it

external_required.name: psycopg2-binary
external_required.role: Postgres driver with SimpleConnectionPool and RealDictCursor

forbidden: Domain-specific interpretation of object_type or label semantics

tables.name: labels.object_labels
columns: label_id text NOT NULL FK labels.labels(id)

persistence.notes: Schema is initialised idempotently at startup. Inline DDL fallback in database.py is kept in sync with the schema.sql artifact for deployments where the sprint folder is absent.

risks.impact: If another component creates a 'labels' schema, the idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS will silently mask conflicts. Schema ownership must be tracked at the infrastructure level.
No cleanup or archival API exists. Stale labels and orphaned attachments (for deleted application objects) accumulate indefinitely and require direct DB maintenance.

GET /api/groups pagination uses ORDER BY object_id for the flat slice. If consuming applications depend on a different stable order, results may appear inconsistent across pages when objects are inserted between page fetches.
